message.content:
Here's a cold email draft you can adapt. I've used placeholders where your specific details go:

---

**Subject:** Quick question about [Prospect Company]'s reporting

Hi [First Name],

I noticed [Prospect Company] is [growing fast / hiring on the data side / expanding into new markets] — congrats. One thing that tends to break first at this stage: getting a straight answer out of your own data usually means waiting on an analyst or a stale spreadsheet.

That's the problem we built [Product Name] to solve. It connects to the tools you already use — [e.g., Stripe, Salesforce, HubSpot] — and turns raw data into live, shareable dashboards in about 15 minutes, with no SQL required. Teams like [Customer A] and [Customer B] typically cut weekly reporting time by [X]% and surfaced [specific win, e.g., "a churn pattern worth ~$40K/mo"] within their first month.

Worth a 20-minute look next week? If you send me a sample export beforehand, I'll build the demo around your actual data — otherwise it's a quick product tour.

Either way, thanks for the read,

[Your Name]
[Title], [Company Name]
[Phone] | [Website]

P.S. If now isn't the right time, I'm happy to send a 2-minute video walkthrough instead — just reply "video."

---

A few notes on the structure: the opener references something specific about the prospect (the #1 driver of cold email reply rates), the middle is one pain point → one solution → one proof point, and the P.S. gives a low-friction fallback CTA.

Since you may act on this draft, let me check my follow-up guidance:
